review: The whole hymn is Psalm 23, so the Hebrew follows the psalm's own wording wherever the Arabic quotes it: רֹעִי / לֹא יֶחְסַר / בִּנְאוֹת דֶּשֶׁא / מֵי מְנוּחֹת / גֵּיא צַלְמָוֶת / שֻׁלְחָן / כּוֹסִי רְוָיָה.
1:4 יַרְבִּיצֵנִי אֵל חַי — the psalm has simply יַרְבִּיצֵנִי; 'the living God' is the Arabic's addition (إِلٰهِي الْحَيّ) and is kept so the line reaches eight syllables.
2:3 וְאֶת־נַפְשִׁי יָשׁוֹב — the psalm reads יְשׁוֹבֵב ('He restores'); the short form is used to keep the line at eight without dropping the verb.
3:4 כִּי־אַתָּה עִמָּדִי — Psalm 23:4 exactly (עִמָּדִי, not עִמִּי), which is also the syllable count the tune needs.

4:1–4:4 — the Arabic separates the staff, the rod and the comfort into four short lines; Hebrew does the same but keeps the psalm's nouns (מִשְׁעֶנֶת, שֵׁבֶט, נִחוּם) so the stanza still reads as Psalm 23:4.
6:2–6:3 מָשַׁחְתָּ רֹאשִׁי / בְּחֶסֶד מִמְּךָ — the psalm has 'You anoint my head with oil'; Hebrew puts the oil in 6:1 and the grace in 6:3, following the Arabic's order.
